In rec.games.deckmaster aahz@hal.COM (Tom Wylie) writes:
>Roberto Ullfig <ullfig@fnrobo.fnal.gov> wrote:
>>a. immediately
>>   if so, then how can a vampire suffer excess aggravated damage?

>I believe it goes into torpor at the end of each strike step...  you don't
>do the damage point by point and check after each to see whether the
>vampire went into torpor.  You pile the damage onto it in one big lump,
>then check for torpor.  This also means it won't stick around for more
>strikes, or to press.

This still does not address a question I asked earlier: namely, what
if both normal and aggravated damage are done in a single strike? I
would argue that the normal damage is applied first, then the
aggravated damage, but the rules don't state. Tom?

(My apologies if this was answered earlier, my news seems to have
expired a bit faster than normal.)

Rollie

Messages.Author: Scowling Jim Cowling
Messages.Body:
In article <33eau7$5ld@fnrobo.fnal.gov>,
Roberto Ullfig <ullfig@fnrobo.fnal.gov> wrote:
>When does a vampire actually go to torpor?
>
>a. immediately
>
>   if so, then how can a vampire suffer excess aggravated damage?

Yes.  How can this happen?  Suppose I have a weapon that does 2 damage,
aggravated.  Or, suppose my minion does aggravated hand damage and I
play a combat card that ups the minion's hand damage.  In either case,
the other minion will go to torpor and lose blood.
